bullets.title: Geopolitical risk-off: Iran strikes drive broad market selloff, 3:1 decliners
bullets.body: US strikes on Iranian military targets near the Strait of Hormuz drove a broad risk-off session with S&P 500 decliners outnumbering gainers 3:1. WTI crude surged 4.4% to $74.25 (Brent ~$80 September futures +8%), gold fell 1.8%, and Bitcoin futures dropped 2.6%. Energy and defensives led; cyclicals, homebuilders (down 4.1%), airlines (down 1.8%), and consumer discretionary lagged sharply.

bullets.title: June FOMC Minutes: hawkish undertones, rate hike probability rising if inflation stays above 3.3%
bullets.body: June FOMC minutes showed hawkish undertones — almost all participants said policy tightening would be warranted if inflation remains elevated, though only 'a few' saw a case for hiking in June. Base case is a gradual shift toward rate hikes around year-end; median 3.3% core PCE aligns with no hikes or one hike, while 3.5% aligns with 2-3 hikes. Front-end rate volatility expected to stay elevated under Chair Warsh; 2-year yields rose 4.4bps to 4.206%, 10-year +4.2bps to 4.571%.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley June CPI preview: headline turns negative on oil, core stable at 2.8%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley forecasts June core CPI at 0.22% m/m (2.8% y/y), roughly in line with May. Headline CPI expected at -0.19% m/m on oil price declines, with y/y at 3.8%. Housing and airfare soften services; core goods tick up modestly.

bullets.title: China H200 approval drives NVDA +3.7%, semis rebound leads tape
bullets.body: China plans to allow top AI firms (Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek) to purchase limited H200 chips (fewer than 200k) following Trump's December approval, restricted to training only. NVDA surged 3.7% and led the semis rebound alongside AVGO; SOX had been down ~14% since June 22 record. JPM notes Mag7 is trading at 10-year lows vs. SPX, maintaining a tactical bullish view.

bullets.title: Hedge funds aggressively cutting AI/momentum longs after worst drawdown since summer 2025
bullets.body: Systematic long-short managers are down 3.6% since June 22 (worst drawdown since summer 2025), with YTD returns falling from 14.4% to 10.8%. Fundamental long-short managers cut AI long exposure that drove their entire YTD alpha through June 22, pushing gross leverage to the bottom decile over the past year. Momentum and crowded AI/Info Tech trades are the primary pain points; the short side of portfolios is worst hit.

bullets.title: Software sector -1.6% on AI disruption fears; semis +2.2% divergence widens
bullets.body: The S&P 500 IT Index gained 1.4% on the day with semiconductors up 2.2% and comm equipment up 3.1% led by AI switch/router names — but software fell 1.6% broadly on AI disruption concerns. Intra-sector rotation risk in tech is elevated given stretched semis valuations; AI exhaustion risk from potential Mag7 capex cuts is cited as the key bear case.

bullets.title: Scotiabank: hyperscaler AI capex concerns misunderstood; power scarcity the real bottleneck
bullets.body: Scotiabank argues the market overweights near-term hyperscaler AI capex concerns and underweights control of scarce compute assets. Power is emerging as the new critical bottleneck as reasoning models increase compute intensity. AMZN (Sector Outperform, $325 PT) and GOOGL (Sector Outperform, $450 PT) are positioned as key beneficiaries; META rated Sector Perform at $700.

bullets.title: Apple-Broadcom $30B+ custom silicon deal through 2031: AVGO +4.8%, meaningful AI ramp 2029/30
bullets.body: Apple and Broadcom announced a $30B+ multiyear agreement through 2031 for custom silicon and wireless connectivity chips, expected to produce 15B+ US-made chips with $1.5B invested in AVGO's Colorado facility. Broadcom's role in custom ASICs for Apple's AI infrastructure will expand meaningfully, though a significant ramp isn't expected until 2029/2030 as Apple's in-house LLM (currently 2-3 years behind frontier models) matures. Citi maintains Buy on both: AAPL PT $315, AVGO PT $500.

bullets.title: NVDA management: roadmap intact, non-hyperscaler momentum building, mid-70s gross margin reaffirmed
bullets.body: Citi's top data center semis pick NVDA confirmed full product roadmap intact despite Kyber/Rubin delays, with NVLink domains unchanged from Computex. Non-hyperscaler demand from AI labs, sovereigns, and enterprises is gaining significant momentum. Blackwell delivers 25x power efficiency vs. Hopper; NVDA targets 50% cash flow return to shareholders. Citi PT $300 (~28x P/E on CY27E EPS of ~$11.90).

bullets.title: PC market: first unit decline in 9 quarters (-4.9% YoY in 2Q26); 2H26 outlook much worse
bullets.body: 2Q26 PC shipments fell 4.9% YoY to 68M units — the first annual decline after 9 consecutive quarters of growth — driven by component shortages in memory and storage as pull-forward demand exhausted. IDC forecasts 2H26 unit declines of 19%; memory shortages expected to persist until early 2028. Revenue continues to rise as vendor price increases outpace unit weakness. Dell share fell to 13.6% from 15.2%; Apple rose to 9.9% from 9.3%.

bullets.title: JPM 5s/30s flattener trade: curve ~20bp too steep, recommends entering ahead of $22B 30-year auction
bullets.body: JPMorgan estimates the 5s/30s Treasury curve is roughly 20bp too steep after adjusting for fundamental drivers including Fed policy, inflation expectations, and balance sheet size. The firm recommends a staged 5s/30s flattener (50% at market, add 50% near 79bp, stop above 85bp) with near-term resistance at 78-82bp. June's 30-year auction cleared 1.2bp cheap to pre-auction levels with end-user demand down 3ppt to 85.3%.

bullets.title: Hotel RevPAR surging: +10.9% YoY week of July 4; luxury +24.5%, World Cup cities +25% avg
bullets.body: US weekly RevPAR jumped 10.9% YoY for the June 28-July 4 period (vs. +9.6% prior week), with luxury up 24.5% — the best week since January 2025. World Cup host markets averaged +25% RevPAR (Kansas City +50%, Philadelphia +39%, Miami +31%). 2Q26 chain-scale beats: HLT +4.7% vs. consensus +3.8%, MAR +5.2% vs. +4.0%, HST +6.9% vs. +3.7%.

bullets.title: Data center REIT valuations fully rerating: further gains must come from earnings, not multiples
bullets.body: US REITs returned +17.6% in 1H 2026, with data centers leading at +31.6% and hotels at +28.9%. However, global real estate now trades at only a 2.5% discount to NAV vs. the 10-year average discount of 10.2%, with forward P/E at 16.7x in line with the 10-year average. UBS flags that the valuation recovery is largely complete; future returns depend on earnings delivery and cash-flow growth rather than further multiple expansion.

bullets.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth to 3% on Mideast war; Airbus slashes 20-year jet demand forecast
bullets.body: The IMF downgraded its 2026 global growth forecast to 3%, citing Middle East war pressures partly offset by AI tailwinds. Airbus cut its 20-year jet demand forecast to 42,060 new aircraft (from 43,400), attributing the revision to the Iran conflict and tariffs. Airlines fell 1.8% sector-wide on crude surge.

bullets.title: Utilities underperform on hawkish Fed; BE -5.7% on Hunterbrook short; EIA sees record power demand
bullets.body: Utilities lagged the S&P 500 amid FOMC minutes signaling possible rate hikes. Bloom Energy fell 5.7% after Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position. The EIA separately forecasts record power demand in 2026-27 driven by commercial sector and data centers, a structural tailwind for the sector despite near-term rate headwinds.

bullets.title: Banking/payments down 2.6-3.0%: Barclays initiates coverage with cautious read on PYPL, WU
bullets.body: The banking sector fell 2.6% and cards/payments 3.0% on Middle East tensions and hawkish Fed signals. Barclays initiated coverage with a broadly cautious tone: PYPL underweight as branded checkout share collapsed from 44% of Visa e-commerce transactions in 2019 to 16% in 2025; WU underweight on rising competition; FISV equal weight after president Suryadevara resigned; GPN equal weight pending high-single-digit revenue acceleration proof.

bullets.title: Tokenized deposits pose structural threat to crypto; de-dollarization trend modestly reversing
bullets.body: JPMorgan warns institutional adoption has favored permissioned blockchains over public chains, and tokenized deposits could reduce stablecoin demand for institutional settlement. Real-world asset tokenization (~$50B market) may concentrate on private rails. Separately, FX reserve managers saw net dollar inflows of ~$25B in 1Q26 — first dollar reserve inflows since 1Q24 — suggesting modest reversal of de-dollarization; central bank gold share of reserves declined from ~31% to just under 28% in 2Q26.

bullets.title: Shopify: bar is high — market needs 30% Q2 rev growth AND mid-to-high 20% Q3 guide to perform
bullets.body: Street expects SHOP Q2 revenue growth of 30-31% and GMV growth of 28-30% with 16% FCF margin. For Q3, consensus ranges from mid-20s to high-20s revenue growth, with some pushing for mid-20s. The analyst view is that the stock requires at least 30% in Q2 and mid-to-high 20% Q3 guidance to work; a deceleration to mid-20% in Q3 would be viewed as too aggressive given tougher comps.

bullets.title: Meta secures 250MW 10-year Alberta power deal for H2 2028 data center; power scarcity theme broadening
bullets.body: Meta entered a greater-than-10-year energy supply agreement with Capital Power Corporation for 250MW to support a new data center in Sturgeon County, Alberta, anticipated in service H2 2028. This adds to the broader theme of hyperscalers locking up long-term contracted power as compute intensity from reasoning AI models creates supply constraints.

bullets.title: US port imports forecasted at record 2.47M TEUs in July on pre-tariff rush
bullets.body: July port imports are expected to hit a record 2.47M TEUs, up 3% y/y, driven by a continued pre-tariff inventory pull-forward. This is a near-term demand signal for logistics and industrials names but also suggests the post-rush demand cliff is approaching.
